capture.final_message:
Represent any affine map \(f:\Bbbk\to E\) as
\[
f(x)=x\smul v+c,
\qquad v=f.\mathrm{linear}(1).
\]
Its increment is exactly
\[
f(x+h)-f(x)=h\smul v,
\]
so at every \(x\) the Fréchet derivative is the continuous linear map \(h\mapsto h\smul v\); the remainder is identically zero. Hence \(f\) is differentiable everywhere, which immediately gives differentiability on every set \(s\) and differentiability at every point \(x\). Organize the conjunction by proving this global differentiability fact once and applying its `differentiableOn` and `differentiableAt` consequences.
